effectiveModel: Uniform deterministic bit algorithm with worst-case running time.

reader.explanation: Number the occurring variables consecutively, discard tautologies and repeated literals, and add two fresh variables forced to opposite values by unit clauses. For each clause, write its satisfying bits in the corresponding positions and fill every other position with one auxiliary symbol. Make one word for each choice of filler. With 2L−1 fillers, at least one filler is absent from any center. Its words force a satisfying bit in each clause, and every satisfying assignment agrees with every word. The two unit clauses ensure that both bits and all fillers occur, so q=2d+3. For n original variables the radius is d=n+1, preserving effective sublinearity, and the encoding has polynomial length.
reader.label: One agreement with a balanced alphabet
